item.title: Drake Gets Surprise Jeff Ross Birthday Roast
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Drake's 40th birthday celebrations continued in Houston, where Jeff Ross surprised him with a roast after his Jim Carrey wish.
item.content:encoded:
Drake’s birthday wish kind of came true when Roastmaster General Jeff Ross surprised him with a roast in Houston.

Ross shared a selfie from the celebration on Instagram Stories. Drake reposted it and called the comic “The F–king General.” The roast footage had not yet appeared online.

The rapper had asked for a different comic in September. After seeing Jim Carrey roast Ross, Drake commented, “Wow this is now all I want for my birthday.”

Carrey’s video marked Ross’ 61st birthday on September 13. The actor joked about Ross’ looks, cast him as an ugly baby and worked a nondisclosure agreement into the gag. Ross welcomed the treatment.

He shared the video with his followers and asked them to add their own insults in the comments.

That exchange put Ross in the position of receiving the kind of jokes he usually tells. His celebrity targets have included Justin Bieber, Tom Brady and Joan Rivers.

He also produced and appeared in Comedy Central’s “Roast Battle,” which ran for three seasons and later aired in other countries.

The Houston stop followed Drake’s New York birthday party, where more than 400 guests gathered and the Backstreet Boys performed.

For Ross, roasting has stretched beyond a guest spot at a star’s party. He teamed with Dave Attell for Netflix’s “Bumping Mics” and created “Historical Roasts,” a six-episode series that applied the format to historical figures.

His solo show, “Take A Banana For The Ride,” brought him to Broadway and later Netflix. That show made Ross himself the subject. He talked about his family and the friends he had lost, including Bob Saget, Norm Macdonald and Gilbert Gottfried.

item.title: 50 Cent Wins Temporary Restraining Order Against Tia Kemp As Battle Over Sons Explodes
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: 50 Cent wins a temporary order against Tia Kemp, restricting her contact with Sire and setting a November 3 court hearing.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent has won a temporary injunction against Tia Kemp limiting her contact with his son.

A Florida judge ordered Kemp to remain at least 500 feet from 14-year-old Sire, according to court documents reviewed by TMZ. The order forbids direct or indirect contact, including messages or posts aimed at the teenager through social media.

Kemp also cannot possess firearms or ammunition under the temporary order and must surrender any weapons after being served. The judge issued the restrictions Monday, granting the rapper’s earlier request.

The initial petition accused Kemp of targeting Sire online across several posts and making claims about his development. The claims about the child’s health have not been established, and the injunction is not a final ruling on them.

50 had objected publicly to using a supposed diagnosis as an insult. “This is the greatest example of bullying a minor saying he is on the spectrum. I have friends who kids are, it’s not a joke.”

His lawyers used stronger language in a separate federal civil complaint. “Ms. Kemp shamelessly used the label ‘on the spectrum’ as a pejorative slur hurled at a child to humiliate him and his family. But autism is not shameful. What is shameful is fabricating a diagnosis for a private child, inventing a sexually degrading cause for it, and broadcasting both to a mass audience.”

50 also alleged Kemp circulated a photo of Sire alongside an explicit image purportedly involving his mother, Daphne Joy. He said she answered a cease-and-desist letter by posting part of it with the caption, “F u and ya lawyers.”

Kemp’s posts followed 50’s mockery of an alleged assault on William Roberts III, her adult son with Rick Ross. Kemp responded publicly to his legal actions and accused him of bullying her.

After filing the separate $6 million lawsuit, 50 wrote, “It’s not ok to bully minors on line, kids have killed them selves over things people have said about them. That gangster granny act is not gonna work no 🏳️ white flags.”

That lawsuit seeks financial damages, while the Florida injunction deals with protection and contact restrictions rather than deciding compensation.

The temporary order expires November 3, when both sides are scheduled to appear before the judge for a possible longer injunction.

item.title: Flavor Flav Writes A Mock Work Excuse For WNBA Finals Fans
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Flavor Flav posted a mock work-excuse note asking bosses to let fans watch Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Flavor Flav offered WNBA fans a signed excuse to miss work for the Finals, asking bosses to let employees miss work for a game scheduled in the middle of the workday.

The Public Enemy rapper posted his mock work note ahead of Thursday’s Game 6 between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream.

“Thursday is a paid holiday. Because Flavor Flav said so,” he wrote. The note requested excused absences and carried his signature, along with the titles “The World’s Greatest Hype Man” and “Official Supporter of Women’s Sports.”

Flav turned his familiar role as a hype man toward fans whose work schedules could keep them from watching. The early start had already drawn complaints from supporters who wanted a prime-time game.

The note followed a much larger effort to celebrate women athletes: his SHE Weekend in Las Vegas. SHE stood for Sports, Hospitality and Entertainment. Held July 16 through 19, the gathering brought about 150 female Winter Olympians and Paralympians to the city.

Flav enlisted companies to help cover the trip. MGM Resorts supplied more than 100 free hotel rooms, Delta Air Lines covered flights, and Dove joined as a sponsor. His fundraiser for the athletes passed $133,000 before the weekend ended.

Public Enemy performed during the celebration, giving athletes time with potential business partners.

The schedule included a parade and a free outdoor concert, followed by meetings that connected athletes with brands and executives. Those sessions put sponsorship opportunities alongside the public festivities.

He also backed Dan Levy on October 12 after the actor challenged Shane Gillis over comments about women’s gym clothes in a “Saturday Night Live” monologue.

Flav shared a report about Levy’s response and added, “Important allyship.” Levy had urged men to speak up about how women were being treated.

Fans planning to watch Thursday: the Valkyries’ official schedule lists Game 6 for October 29 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Tipoff is at 12:30 P.M. Eastern, and USA and Peacock will air the game.

item.title: Drake, 21 Savage, Travis Scott Rumors Circulate, But Feel Shaky
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Drake’s relationships with 21 Savage and Future are in question in a viral birthday rumor.
item.content:encoded:
Drake might need a friendship audit after his birthday celebration. Do not shoot the messenger. I am only repeating what I saw and filing the quota for the day.

The dude Adam22 is talking a bit and it is going somewhat viral. I am clearly getting this second or third hand.

According to the account provided, Adam says a source at the party suggested things may be shaky between Drake, 21 Savage and Future. That is somebody’s assessment, so keep the verdict tucked away for now.

With 21, homeboy’s argument only involves absence, missing Instagram likes and some other company. He says Drake and 21 haven’t been liking each other’s recent posts. This is the definition of Chatty Patty activity. Now, 21 was spending time with Metro Boomin during the birthday festivities. We know Metro took it to Drake’s chest at one point. Adam’s comments are hardly proof of a disagreement.

Personally, I need more than an unemployed heart button before declaring a friendship deceased. LOL! These men could have an issue. We already know this. They could also have conversations Instagram is not privy to.

Now, Future is already down with Drake, right?n They have a new song!

Ol’ Adam says his source believes Future and Drake remain on questionable terms despite that recent activity. Future allegedly isn’t prepared to stop associating with everybody Drake has problems with. And that is a rumor that suggests there is friction. I had no idea rappers had friendship agreements. Is that a FDA? Friends Disclosure Agreement?

The Travis Scott portion gets even less credible. Adam says he saw Travis at the celebration but never witnessed him connect with Drake. He was not there though. So, what does this even mean. Future and Travis are apparently working on new music and used the party as a jumpoff spot.

“It kind of feels like they pulled up almost with a MALICIOUS INTENT.”

That is quite an accusation to attach to an alleged party relocation.

Anyway, there are others that are saying that Future and Travis were not both there. Actually, people are saying both did not attend, saying Travis may have reached the door. And was actually at a separate event. Attendance itself remains contested. I mean….this is why the source matters.

For AllHipHop readers keeping score, this about as a shaky of a rumor I will ever write. This is like thirdhand and secondhand information.

LeSigh.

item.title: Nicki Minaj White House Rumor Gets Four-Word Answer From Gavin Newsom’s Office
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Nicki Minaj's White House press secretary rumor drew a four-word reply from Gavin Newsom's press office amid their ongoing dispute.
item.content:encoded:
Gavin Newsom’s press office had four words for the prospect of Nicki Minaj becoming Donald Trump’s next White House press secretary: “We can only pray.”

The California governor’s team posted the reply on X in response to reports about White House staffers floating the rapper for the job. Newsom’s office also responded to Trump’s remarks about Minaj’s backside, posting: “An unlikely match. Then again, it all Depends.”

The rapper traveled with the president to Michigan and appeared at his rally as he campaigned for Republicans ahead of the November 3 midterms.

The job speculation grew out of an October 25 exchange with White House communications director Steven Cheung. AllHipHop previously covered his playful interview with Minaj aboard Air Force One, where he asked her about the economy, Trump’s campaign schedule and polling.

“Ladies and gentlemen, I think we may have found the new White House Press Secretary!” Cheung wrote with the video.

Nicki Minaj shared Cheung’s post with an American flag and a sweating emoji. She praised Trump’s business experience and argued that his recovery from personal financial trouble gave her confidence in how he would handle the country’s finances.

She also praised his stamina on the campaign trail and his willingness to help other Republicans win elections.

The White House job talk followed Katie Zacharia’s five-day stint as press secretary in October and Karoline Leavitt’s departure in August.

Nicki Minaj had criticized Newsom at a Turning Point USA event in December 2025, where she appeared with Erika Kirk. In a TIME interview, she said she sought the governor’s help after swatting incidents at her home and received no reply.

“He just completely ignored me, with all the money I spent in taxes,” Minaj told TIME.

The magazine said Newsom’s office did not respond to its request for comment. Minaj said Florida Rep. Anna Paulina Luna later helped connect her with federal law enforcement and a private security firm.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Plans Halloween Cannabis Expansion
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa planned a Halloween arrival for Khalifa Kush in New York, with a local partner and 36 dispensaries in the rollout.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa lined up a Halloween launch for Khalifa Kush in New York, with 36 dispensaries in the company’s plans and years of requests behind the move.

DJ Saul, the brand’s CEO, told amNewYork Metro that New York had drawn more requests than any other market. He said Wiz visited the state at least a couple of times each year.

“New York has been asking for KK for years and years now,” Saul said.

The October 31 debut will include seven New York City locations. The opening lineup pairs the KK and Violet Sky strains with flower and pre-rolls.

Khalifa Kush placed the other 29 planned locations in upstate New York and Long Island.

Saul described a business built around the cannabis Wiz himself smokes. He told amNewYork that the brand started 15 years ago with a strain developed around the rapper’s tastes, then grew from medical cannabis into recreational sales.

Saul said Wiz’s role went beyond lending his name to a cannabis company. He tied the brand’s identity to the rapper using its product himself, a distinction he emphasized while discussing celebrity business deals.

Skyworld will grow and distribute Khalifa Kush’s New York products. On its website, the company describes itself as Indigenous-owned and identifies SJR Horticulture, LLC as its operator. It lists licenses for cultivation, processing and distribution. Its site also links to lab results and identifies indoor cultivation as part of its business.

The expansion follows a decade of deals that put Wiz’s name into the regulated cannabis business. In February 2016, AllHipHop reported his agreement with Colorado’s RiverRock Cannabis, described then as his first collaboration in that industry. That arrangement covered the development and production of strains he curated, infused products and concentrates.

RiverRock planned its launch for April 20 that year, including Khalifa Kush flower and concentrates. Wiz also renewed his separate agreement with RAW Rolling Papers around that time, adding products to an accessories partnership. The Colorado agreement dealt with cannabis production while the RAW deal covered items used with it, giving his business more than one route into the market.

New York would become Khalifa Kush’s 14th U.S. market, the company said in its announcement.

item.title: Roger Goodell Explains Jay-Z’s Super Bowl Timing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jay-Z had his Super Bowl vision ready, Roger Goodell said as he explained why the rapper finally accepted the halftime show.
item.content:encoded:
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said Jay-Z had a vision for his Super Bowl halftime show as he explained why the rapper finally accepted the gig.

Goodell discussed the decision during an October 27 interview with Ebro Darden and Eddie Francis on Apple Music’s “The Ebro Show.”

He said Jay had put off the performance before telling him, “I wanna do it this year. I think he’s already got his vision; he already understands what he wants to do,” Goodell said.

The commissioner linked the timing to Jay’s anniversary year, completed tour and the Los Angeles setting.

The booking will bring him back to SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, 2027. The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced the headlining slot on October 26.

It will be his first Super Bowl halftime performance after years of helping shape the event for other artists.

In the official announcement, Goodell said he had asked Jay to perform when the league first agreed to work with Roc Nation. He left the timing to the rapper. Their partnership began in 2019, with Roc Nation taking a role in the NFL’s music entertainment.

That work will continue while its founder performs.

Roc Nation will executive produce the Super Bowl LXI halftime telecast and serve as strategic entertainment advisor for the live show. Hamish Hamilton will direct it. The game will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+, with mobile viewing through NFL+.

SoFi also hosted the 2022 halftime show, when Dr. Dre led a lineup that included Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige and Kendrick Lamar.

The return to SoFi follows Jay’s October 23 and 24 anniversary concerts there.

Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort joined the final night, while Friday’s guests included Scarface, John Legend and DJ Khaled. Blue Ivy Carter also played piano during her father’s first show.

Those concerts celebrated 30 years of Reasonable Doubt and 25 years of The Blueprint.

The run took Jay through New York, London and Paris before finishing in Los Angeles. At Saturday’s finale, he also honored Nipsey Hussle with an on-screen tribute and worked the late rapper’s music into the set.

item.title: Twista’s Federal Tax Sentencing Reportedly Delayed Until 2027
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Chicago Hip-Hop veteran Twista reportedly has more time before learning his fate in federal court.
item.content:encoded:
Twista will apparently have to wait a little longer to find out whether he will serve prison time in connection with his federal tax case.

The legendary Chicago rapper, whose real name is Carl Mitchell, was originally scheduled to be sentenced on October 22, 2026, after pleading guilty to five misdemeanor counts of willfully failing to pay federal income taxes.

READ ALSO: Twista & City Winery Join Forces In New York To Celebrate Legacy…

However, according to federal tax attorney Rick Yandle, the sentencing has been postponed twice and is now reportedly scheduled for January 20, 2027.

The reason for the reported delays has not been independently confirmed. The revised date also has not been verified through the latest federal court docket.

Twista’s legal troubles stem from his failure to pay federal income taxes over multiple years, specifically from 2019 through 2023.

According to federal prosecutors, the rapid-fire rapper earned substantial income during that period but failed to satisfy his federal tax obligations.

As part of his plea agreement, Twista agreed to pay $441,059.91 in restitution.

Although the charges are misdemeanors, the potential consequences are serious. Each count carries a maximum sentence of one year in federal prison, meaning Twista theoretically faces up to five years behind bars if the maximum penalties were imposed consecutively.

Yandle’s analysis indicates that the estimated advisory sentencing range is 12 to 18 months. However, that range is not a guarantee of incarceration, and the judge retains discretion when determining the appropriate punishment.

The case represents an unusual legal chapter for one of Chicago’s most respected Hip-Hop figures.

Twista, who rose to national prominence through his lightning-fast delivery, became a household name with hits like “Slow Jamz” featuring Kanye West and Jamie Foxx, as well as “Overnight Celebrity.” His influence on Midwest Hip-Hop and rapid-fire lyricism has endured for decades.

The reported postponement means the veteran MC could enter 2027 with his legal future still unresolved.

The Internal Revenue Service’s public announcement continues to identify October 22 as the original sentencing date, while Yandle’s published analysis points to the January hearing.

For now, no sentence has been publicly confirmed, and it remains unclear whether Twista will ultimately receive incarceration, probation or another penalty.

item.title: Armani Caesar Says Pregnancy Reveal Cost Her 50,000 Followers
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Armani Caesar said she lost about 50,000 followers after revealing her pregnancy as motherhood changed her approach to music.
item.content:encoded:
Armani Caesar said she lost about 50,000 followers after revealing her pregnancy, even as motherhood pushed her to rethink what she wanted to say in her music.

The Buffalo rapper recalled the reaction on an episode of Angela Yee’s “Lip Service”, released October 27.

“My phone was going crazy. The comments was in shambles. I lost like 50,000 followers,” she said.

She described her following as mostly male. But her own priorities had shifted toward her daughter and the example she wanted to set. Being pretty or being a boss wasn’t all she wanted her child to value. Integrity mattered, too, and she wanted that growth to show up in her songs.

On “Lip Service,” Caesar said working with a small team while juggling music, touring and her boutique had left her burned out. She also described a more personal approach to her next project, including writing about postpartum struggles and problems in her private life.

Her public image had long included both rap and fashion. In a 2022 SHEEN interview, she explained that her boutique, Armani’s Closet, grew from the outfits and photos she was already sharing. Turning that interest into a business gave her another job to manage alongside recording.

The workload was already a topic then. Asked how she handled both businesses, she said she was still learning to divide her time and had brought in more help.

By that point, her music career had taken her to Coachella, Rolling Loud, Day N Vegas and Made in America. She told SHEEN those performances were also her first visits to the festivals, putting her onstage at events she had never attended as a fan.

That run followed her 2020 signing to Griselda, where she became the label’s first female rapper. Westside Gunn welcomed a fellow Buffalo artist whose connection to the crew went back more than a decade.

She released The Liz in 2020, followed by The Liz 2 in 2022. The 17-track follow-up included Westside Gunn, Benny The Butcher and Conway The Machine, plus Kodak Black on “Diana.” She had reached out to Kodak herself through a direct message to set up their collaboration.

item.title: Jay-Z & Roc Nation Step Up For 3-Year-Old Soccer Star After Police Called
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Jay-Z and Roc Nation help lil' Nevada Pierre secure a promising European opportunity as an extraordinary preschool athlete has attracted powerful allies.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z and Roc Nation Sports are reportedly sending 3-year-old soccer sensation Nevada Pierre to Spain after a controversial youth soccer dispute in Florida brought police to the field and turned the toddler into a national sensation.

What began as an ugly disagreement at a recreational soccer game could now open international doors for the unusually talented youngster.

According to Loren LoRosa of “The Breakfast Club,” Jay-Z and Roc Nation Sports have committed to sending Nevada to Spain in December 2026 for an athletic experience intended to encourage his development. The plans reportedly include working with the family to make the trip meaningful for the aspiring soccer player. Yahoo Sports

The reported offer marks an extraordinary reversal for Nevada, whose family found itself confronting police just days earlier over a dispute involving his participation in a children’s soccer league.

On Oct. 24, officers responded to Martin Luther King Jr. Park in Winter Park, Florida, after an official with i9 Sports requested assistance following a confrontation involving Nevada’s parents, Martasia Griffin and Don Pierre.

The parents alleged their son was being penalized because he was simply too skilled for the competition, which included children older than him.

Videos circulating online showed Nevada maneuvering around opponents and scoring goals with remarkable confidence for a child his age.

However, league officials offered a different account.

An official acknowledged Nevada’s advanced abilities but alleged he had pushed other children during the game. The official also accused his parents of disruptive behavior following disagreements about playing time.

The Winter Park Police Department subsequently clarified that officers responded to a dispute involving adults rather than the child’s athletic abilities. No arrests were made and authorities classified the situation as a civil matter. Yahoo Sports+1

The disagreement nevertheless ignited a national conversation about how youth sports programs accommodate unusually talented children and how conflicts between parents and administrators should be handled.

Former U.S. national soccer player Eddie Johnson also entered the picture, offering to train Nevada through his EJE7 Soccer Academy in Orlando.

Johnson criticized what he described as longstanding barriers within youth soccer, particularly for children of color.

“We should be praising a three year old with his ability instead of tarnishing it,” Johnson wrote on social media. Dayton’s BIN 1340

Meanwhile, Nevada’s family established a GoFundMe campaign to help cover training, equipment, registration and travel expenses.

Griffin told Orlando television station WKMG that the campaign had raised more than $40,000 as support poured in from people following her son’s experience. WKMG

The attention has also taken an emotional toll. Griffin said Nevada was frightened by the police encounter and worried about being removed from another soccer program.

Now, with Roc Nation Sports reportedly preparing an overseas opportunity and Johnson offering professional guidance, Nevada’s future looks considerably different from the uncertain scene that unfolded on that Florida field.
